data.say: I confirm the Thursday text notice, quiet after 10pm, and my 6pm stove slot, and since neither of us has a smoking or budget conflict, I see us as a strong match.

highlights: No smoking conflict: both want a non-smoking household and listed no smoking indoors as a non-negotiable. Both also love pets but have none, so there is no pet friction.

Money is closely aligned. Both agreed on equal utilities, split basics (including dish soap, paper towels and trash bags), own food kept separate, Splitwise with monthly settlement, and a deposit of up to one month's rent ($1,360). The $1,360 share is within Rohan's $1,100-1,400 hard cap.

Routines mesh well. Both rate cleanliness 4 and want a rotating chore chart. Both prefer 68-72°F and shower 15-30 minutes, and they resolved the bathroom overlap (Rohan before 7am, Sofia from 7am). Kitchen use is staggered (Rohan ~6pm, Sofia after 7:30pm). Both are students who leave daily, and both want a 1-year lease and a 1-3 month move-in.
concerns: Guest frequency differs. Rohan hosts never or very rarely and sleeps before 10pm. Sofia hosts weekly, with her partner most Fridays, and small gatherings under 10. Rohan accepted this conditionally (Thursday text notice, quiet after 10pm), so repeated lapses could cause resentment.

Social energy differs. Sofia rates herself 4 (extroverted) and prioritizes matching social energy. Rohan prefers quiet and respect for quiet time, and his headphones comment suggests he is tolerating rather than enjoying the noise. Sofia also admits to noise a few times a week.

Budget headroom is thin. Rohan's hard cap is $1,400, and the $1,360 share leaves only about $40 of room. Sofia's partner staying most Fridays may also nudge utility use up. The conversation never clarified whether $1,360 includes utilities or what happens if the rent rises.
middle_ground: Put the guest rules in writing: Thursday text notice for Friday overnight guests, quiet after 10pm, parties under 10 only on weekends with advance notice, and no weeknight parties. Review after the first 60 days.

Confirm in writing that the $1,360 share, plus the expected utility share, stays under Rohan's $1,400 cap. Agree that any rent or utility increase beyond the cap triggers a conversation, and consider capping the number of overnight stays per month or having the partner chip in on utilities if stays go beyond Fridays.
analysis.recommendation_summary: Rohan and Sofia share the one non-negotiable they have in common (no indoor smoking), and Rohan's budget cap is respected. They reached explicit agreement on money, cleanliness, bathroom, kitchen and guest logistics. The main risk is the gap between Sofia's weekly social life and Rohan's early-bedtime, quiet-seeking habits, which the agreed guest rules should manage.
